key_insight: Metal Sandbox combines isolated file access and native macOS command execution to support concurrent AI agents developing Apple Metal kernels. It targets GPU idle time that occurs while agents wait for model responses or run development commands.
problem_solved: GPU coding agents need native Apple Silicon tools, but their workflows alternate between GPU work and non-GPU tasks. Supporting multiple agents therefore requires both execution isolation and coordination of shared GPU access.
method: Restrict each agent instance’s file access to isolate concurrent development sessions.
Execute development commands natively on macOS to support Apple Metal tooling.
Coordinate work at the command level; the provided abstract is truncated before scheduling details or evaluation results.
impact: This infrastructure could help practitioners train and evaluate Metal kernel-generating agents while making better use of local Apple Silicon GPUs. The provided excerpt does not establish measured performance gains.

paper_title: Metal Sandbox: Isolated Execution and Command Scheduling for GPU Coding Agents on Apple Silicon
paper_authors: Haozhe Wang, Lina Chen, Fanqi Wan, Qi Han, Yinmin Zhang
